evals.prompt: Here's the business case for moving our three regional finance teams into one shared services centre. Help me understand what's actually changing and write it up.
evals.expected_output: Extracts why, what is changing, what is not changing, who is broadly affected, key dates, success in business terms, decisions and constraints, and open questions from the business case; proposes a short initiative name; shows an answer-first summary and waits for yes before writing docs/change/scope.md.
assertions: Covers what is NOT changing, or flags it as a gap if the source is silent
States success as business outcomes, not project milestones
Lists open questions, each with who can answer it
Proposes an initiative name and asks the user to confirm it
Shows a summary and waits for yes before writing

evals.prompt: I don't have a business case, just a two-line email from the COO saying we're moving to a hub model by Q3. Scope the change.
evals.expected_output: Runs a short interview or works from the email, marks unknowns as assumptions, does not invent benefits, dates or headcounts, and records the missing business case as an open question.
assertions: Does not invent benefits, figures, dates or headcounts
Marks unsupported statements as [ASSUMPTION — confirm with ...]
Records the missing business case or success measures as an open question
Keeps status as draft and names project and business owners for validation

evals.prompt: Scope the change for the firewall rule update going to CAB tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as IT change control, says so in one line, and does not produce a change definition.
assertions: Identifies the request as IT/ITIL change control
